title: Croquetas de Jamón
subtitle: Spanish ham croquettes with a creamy béchamel filling
excerpt: Croquetas de jamón are the most popular Spanish tapa: small, oval croquettes with a rich, creamy béchamel filling studded with finely chopped ham, coated in breadcrumbs and fried until golden. The filling is made ahead and chilled until firm, then shaped, breaded, and fried.
sourceNotes: Croquetas are ubiquitous in Spanish bars and restaurants. While versions exist in many European cuisines, the Spanish croqueta has a distinctive long, oval shape and a very soft, barely set béchamel interior, far creamier than most French or British versions. Jamón serrano or jamón ibérico are the classic fillings, though ham cooked is widely used at home.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze after breading but before frying. Fry directly from frozen, adding 2 minutes to cooking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Makes a large batch. Scale up the béchamel in direct proportion.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling must be made at least 3 hours before shaping, or up to 2 days ahead.

content.text: The béchamel for croquetas is much stiffer than a sauce béchamel: it holds its shape when cold. The ratio is much more flour and butter relative to milk than standard béchamel. It will look over-thickened on the hob. That is correct. The filling should be so firm after chilling that you can slice it cleanly.

items.prepNote: 80 g for the béchamel, 50 g for dusting the croquetas before coating

content.text: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes until the mixture is golden and smells nutty. Remove from the heat.

Add the hot milk in a steady stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Return to medium heat and cook, whisking, for 8 to 10 minutes until the mixture is very thick and leaves the sides of the pan. Season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg. Stir in the ham.
Pour the filling into a shallow dish, smoothing the top. Press cling film directly onto the surface. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours until completely firm.
Set up three bowls: flour, beaten egg, panko. Shape tablespoons of cold filling into oval shapes. Dust in flour, dip in egg, then roll in panko. Set on a tray.
Heat the oil in a deep saucepan to 180°C. Fry the croquetas in batches of 4 to 5 for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Filling was not firm enough, coating was not complete, or oil was too hot
items.fix: Chill the filling completely. It should feel rigid when pressed. Ensure every part of the croqueta is sealed in the breadcrumb coating, with no gaps. Oil at 180°C gives the crust time to set before the centre melts.
